events.title: Noah Smith publishes critique of "$140,000 poverty line" claim
events.summary: Noah Smith published an essay on Noahpinion critiquing asset manager Mike Green's argument that the real poverty line for a family of four should be $140,000 rather than the official $31,200. Smith identifies two main problems: Green uses incorrect data (confusing food-at-home spending of 7% with total food spending of 12.9%, and comparing family-of-four income to household income that includes single-person households), and Green's methodology fundamentally misdefines poverty by extrapolating from middle-class spending patterns rather than poor-household spending patterns. Smith argues the claim is contradicted by empirical evidence showing most Americans have adequate food, shelter, health insurance, and transportation.
events.why_relevant: The event documents a public intellectual's detailed rebuttal of a widely-circulated claim about poverty measurement, illustrating how misinformation about economic conditions can spread through media and the importance of fact-checking in public discourse.

events.summary: The New York City Council introduced legislation to ban the use of PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) in protective turnout gear worn by the city's 11,000 firefighters. events.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency published a notice of availability and request for public comment on an Updated Draft Risk Calculation Memorandum for formaldehyde under the Toxic Substances Control Act. events.title: Case update — Cathy A. Harris v. Bessent et al (D.C. Cir.) 25-5037
events.summary: The D.C. Circuit ruled 2-1 that firing protections for members of the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) and Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB) are unconstitutional. In the decision, Judge Gregory Katsas, joined by Judge Justin Walker, wrote that the NLRB and MSPB wield executive, rather than quasi-legislative or quasi-judicial power, and that Congress thus cannot restrict the president from removing their members. In dissent, Judge Florence Pan wrote that, until and unless the Supreme Court overturns Humphrey's Executor , which deemed firing protections for heads of independent multimember agencies constitutional, that case “requires us to uphold the independence of the MSPB and the NLRB.”

Autism advocates immediately mobilized, with organizations including the Association of University Centers on Disabilities, the Autistic Self Advocacy Network, and others demanding that public health officials "listen to autistic voices" and launching communications campaigns to counter the misinformation and maintain public confidence in vaccines.

events.title: CNN reports boat was not headed for U.S., contradicting administration claim
events.summary: CNN reported that the boat struck on September 2 was not headed for the United States, contradicting a claim made by President Trump. Admiral Frank "Mitch" Bradley, overseeing Special Operations that day, told Congress the intelligence indicated the boat was headed to meet a larger vessel bound for Suriname to transfer drugs. Bradley confirmed the military could not locate the second vessel. U.S. drug enforcement officials stated that drugs trafficked through Suriname are generally bound for Europe. Bradley also confirmed that after the people on the boat appeared to see American aircraft, they turned the boat back toward land.
events.why_relevant: The reporting reveals that the administration's public justification for the strike—that the boat was headed toward the U.S.—was inaccurate, undermining the stated rationale for military action without congressional authorization.

events.title: New York Times reports survivors of first strike were waving before second strike
events.summary: Journalists Julian E. Barnes and Charlie Savage reported that survivors of the first strike on the boat were waving to something overhead before a second strike killed them. The report notes that the administration had not announced its new policy of striking alleged drug traffickers rather than arresting them, so the men had no way of knowing they were under attack. Some observers believed the men were waving to be rescued; others supporting the administration's position speculated they were signaling other alleged traffickers, though no other vessels or aircraft were in visual range.
events.why_relevant: The reporting reveals potential evidence that the strike may have targeted individuals attempting to surrender or seek rescue rather than active combatants, raising questions about the legality and proportionality of the military action.
events.basis: those who have seen the video reported that the two survivors of the first strike were waving to something overhead before the second strike killed them.

events.title: Trump administration released 2025 National Security Strategy
events.summary: The Trump administration released its 2025 National Security Strategy late on December 5, 2025, marking a dramatic departure from post-World War II U.S. foreign policy. events.title: Pentagon announces lethal strike on boat in eastern Pacific, killing four men
events.summary: The US military, at the direction of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, conducted a lethal kinetic strike on a vessel in international waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing four men described as narco-terrorists. The strike, the 22nd such operation since September, was conducted by Joint Task Force Southern Spear and targeted a boat suspected of carrying illegal narcotics. The operation brings the death toll of the campaign to at least 87 people. The strike occurs amid mounting congressional scrutiny over the legal basis for the attacks.
events.why_relevant: The strike exemplifies escalating extrajudicial military operations against suspected drug smugglers in international waters, raising constitutional and international law questions about executive authority, rules of engagement, and the lawfulness of killing individuals without due process or clear armed-conflict status.
events.basis: Joint Task Force Southern Spear conducted a lethal kinetic strike on a vessel in international waters operated by a Designated Terrorist Organization. Four male narco-terrorists aboard the vessel were killed.

events.title: TPUSA operations head posts about sinking narco boats; Hegseth responds with video of homicide
events.summary: Andrew Kolvet, who now runs operations at Turning Point USA after Charlie Kirk's death, posted on social media: "Every new attack aimed at Pete Hegseth makes me want another narco drug boat blown up and sent to the bottom of the ocean." Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth responded: "Your wish is our command, Andrew. Just sunk another narco boat," and posted a video of what the bulletin describes as "another homicide committed by DOD." A 23-year-old Pentagon correspondent named Lance Johnston then posted: "Absolutely no laws were broken in 'Signal Gate'. No classified information was leaked whatsoever. Fantastic news for security!"
events.why_relevant: The Secretary of Defense publicly boasted about military action in response to a political supporter's post, and posted video evidence of a killing, raising questions about the politicization of military operations and the treatment of potential homicides as political messaging.
events.basis: Hegseth responded: 'Your wish is our command, Andrew. Just sunk another narco boat.' He then posted the video of another homicide committed by DOD.

events.title: Afghan man shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C.
events.summary: An Afghan national shot and killed two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C., an incident that prompted debate over whether Afghan refugees should be collectively blamed or judged as a group for the act of one individual.
events.why_relevant: A violent attack by an individual of Afghan origin became the factual predicate for political arguments about collective judgment of Afghan refugees and national-origin-based immigration policy, illustrating how individual violence is used to justify group-based restrictions.
events.basis: the Afghan man who shot two National Guardsmen in Washington, D.C. a week ago
